facts.statement: Haopterus fossils date back 124.6 million years.
facts.quote: Its fossil remains dated back 124.6 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus Haopterus was named in 2001 by Wang Xiaolin and Lü Junchang.
facts.quote: It was in 2001 named by Wang Xiaolin and Lü Junchang.

facts.statement: The genus is based on holotype IVPP V11726, a crushed fossil discovered in 1998 at the Sihetun locality.
facts.quote: The genus is based on holotype IVPP V11726, a crushed fossil found in 1998 at the Sihetun-locality.

facts.statement: Haopterus was the first Chinese pterosaur fossil to preserve a skull.
facts.quote: It was the first Chinese pterosaur fossil preserving the skull.

facts.statement: Haopterus had a low skull 145 mm long that lacked a crest.
facts.quote: The skull of Haopterus is with a length of 145 mm long and low, lacking a crest.

facts.statement: The teeth of Haopterus were robust, sharp, pointed, and curved backwards.
facts.quote: The teeth are robust, sharp, pointed, and curving backwards.

facts.statement: The estimated wingspan of the type individual was 1.35 meters.
facts.quote: The wingspan of the type individual was estimated at 1.35 meter (4.43 ft).

facts.statement: Haopterus had weakly built hindlimbs with metatarsals only 17 mm long.
facts.quote: In comparison, the hindlimbs must have been weakly built, the metatarsal having a length of just 17 mm.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that Haopterus moved quadrupedally on land and lived a piscivorous lifestyle as a specialized soarer.
facts.quote: The authors concluded that its slender hindfeet meant that it was forced to move quadrupedally on land, suggesting a piscivore lifestyle as a specialised soarer.

facts.statement: An analysis by Kellner et al. in 2019 showed Haopterus to be a close relative of Mimodactylus.
facts.quote: Later, an analysis by Kellner et al., 2019 showed Haopterus to be a close relative of Mimodactylus.

facts.statement: Haopterus and Mimodactylus form the family Mimodactylidae, which is the sister group to the Istiodactylidae.
facts.quote: Together they form the family Mimodactylidae, which is the sister group to the Istiodactylidae.

facts.statement: Haopterus lived during the Barremian-Aptian age of the Lower Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Haopterus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Barremian-Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Haopterus lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
